Usage: klar variants [options] <color>

Generate a grid of color variants (adaptive deltaE spacing by default)

Arguments:
  color                  Base color (hex, rgb, oklch)

Options:
  --min-delta <n>        Minimum Delta E 2000 between vertically adjacent cells
                         in a column, adaptive mode only (default: 11)
  --light-steps <n>      Fixed lightness steps (disables adaptive mode)
  --chroma-steps <n>     Fixed chroma steps (disables adaptive mode)
  --color-space <space>  oklch or hsl (hsl forces fixed-step mode) (default:
                         "oklch")
  --json                 Output as JSON (default: false)
  -h, --help             display help for command

Default mode (adaptive): each column holds one chroma, and the grid
self-sizes so vertically adjacent cells in a column differ by at least
--min-delta (11 by default). Cells side by side in a row differ in
chroma and are not held to that floor. Every cell emitted is in gamut.

  $ klar variants "#3b82f6"
  $ klar variants "#ff6600" --min-delta 15
  $ klar variants "#3b82f6" --json

Fixed-step mode (explicit --light-steps / --chroma-steps): divides the
space uniformly and is NOT gamut-aware — cells outside sRGB come back as
"color": "", and they are often the majority (--light-steps 10
--chroma-steps 5 on a saturated blue yields 50 cells, 36 of them empty).
Filter them out before use; passing "" to another klar command is an
error. Prefer adaptive mode unless you need fixed dimensions.

  $ klar variants "#3b82f6" --light-steps 10 --chroma-steps 5
  $ klar variants "#3b82f6" --color-space hsl --light-steps 5 --chroma-steps 3
  $ klar variants "#3b82f6" --light-steps 4 --chroma-steps 3 --json | jq -r '.[][] | select(.color != "") | .color'
Usage: klar contrast [options] <foreground> <background>

Calculate contrast between a foreground and a background. OKCA is polarity-aware
— argument order matters (some plugins are too).

Arguments:
  foreground            Foreground color (hex, rgb, oklch)
  background            Background color (hex, rgb, oklch)

Options:
  -t, --type <type>     Algorithm: okca, wcag2, deltaE (built-in), plus any
                        installed contrast-algorithm plugins (default: "okca")
  --gamut-map <method>  Out-of-gamut resolution: css (CSS Color 4 chroma
                        reduction), clip (clamp each channel into range), none
                        (measure the authored color; unavailable for algorithms
                        whose domain it exceeds) (default: "css")
  --allow-out-of-gamut  Exit 0 instead of 1 when an input is outside the gamut
                        (default: false)
  --json                Output as JSON (default: false)
  -q, --quiet           Print only the numeric value (default: false)
  -h, --help            display help for command

Out-of-gamut colors:
  A color authored in OKLCH can sit outside sRGB. It has to be resolved to a
  displayable color before it can be measured, so the reported number describes
  that mapped equivalent — not the color in your token file. That is a real
  answer to a different question, so it exits 1 rather than passing silently.
  Pass --allow-out-of-gamut to accept it, or read gamut.outOfGamut from --json.

  Reducing chroma is the fix, but the number will not move until the color is
  actually in gamut: chroma reduction maps every out-of-gamut chroma at a given
  lightness and hue onto the same boundary color.

  KLAR_GAMUT_MAP sets the default mapping process-wide. No environment
  variable waives the failure — that decision belongs at the call site.

Examples:
  $ klar contrast "#fff" "#000"
  $ klar contrast "#fff" "#000" --type wcag2
  $ klar contrast "oklch(50% 0.2 240)" "#000" -q
  $ klar contrast "oklch(0.79 0.22 25)" "#070e16" --json
  $ klar contrast "oklch(0.79 0.22 25)" "#070e16" --allow-out-of-gamut -q
  $ klar contrast "#fff" "#000" --type okca --json

content.text:
I ran `klar variants "#3b82f6" --light-steps 4 --chroma-steps 3`. Only 3 of the 12 cells came back as real colors, so the grid below has gaps. I measured each real cell with `klar contrast <cell> "#ffffff"` (OKCA, foreground on white, body-text threshold 4.5).

| Lightness (OKLCH L) | Chroma 0.078 | Chroma 0.188 | Chroma 0.298 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.873 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.623 | `#6b88b6` (2.9, fail) | `#3b82f6` (2.9, fail) | out of gamut |
| 0.373 | `#274069` (9.2, pass) | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.123 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |

- **Passes body text on white:** only `#274069`, at 9.2.
- **Fails:** `#6b88b6` and `#3b82f6`, both at 2.9. Your base color doesn't pass for body text on white.
- **Why the gaps:** fixed-step mode isn't gamut-aware, so the 9 cells outside sRGB come back with an empty `color` value. I didn't measure them. Any cell in the top row (too light) or bottom row (too dark) at this hue is out of gamut.

Adaptive mode (the default) only returns in-gamut cells, but it can't give exactly 4x3. It gives 7 rows by 3 columns at the default min-delta of 11, with the higher-chroma columns shorter. Do you want that instead? I can run OKCA on every cell in it and mark which pass. I can also use `klar find` to get a passing shade of #3b82f6 for white text.
